figures.caption: Amino acid sequence analysis of CFEM domain-containing proteins in IK726. A Schematic presentation of CFEM domain organisation, presence of signal peptide, and transmembrane domains. B Multiple sequence alignment of amino acid sequences of IK726 CFEM domain-containing proteins with already characterised B. cinerea (BC1G_15201), S. sclerotiorum (SS1G_07295), T. gamsii (TGAM01_v206178) and F. graminearum (FGSG_03599) proteins showing conserved Cys residues. C Graphical representation of consensus sequences. Sequence Logos were generated using WelLogo (http://weblogo.berkeley.edu/logo.cgi. The height of each sequence corresponds to its conservation. * Indicates putative effectors, # indicates putative antimicrobial activity
figures.label: Fig. 1

figures.caption: Heatmap showing expression profiles of IK726 CFEM genes during interactions with B. cinerea (Cr-Bc) or R. Solani (Cr-Rs), at before contact (BC) and after contact (AC) interaction stages. IK726, confronted with itself, was used as control (Cr-Cr). Relative expression level based on RT-qPCR was calculated as the ratio between the target cfem and actin gene using 2−ΔΔCt method [20] and compared with the Cr-Cr BC. Error bars represent standard deviation of five biological replicates. * ** or *** indicates statistically significant differences with a P > 0.05, P > 0.01 or P > 0.001 in gene expression between treatments based on Fisher’s exact test, and ns indicates no significant difference
figures.label: Fig. 2

figures.caption: Purification and analysis of antimicrobial activity of CFEM10. A Sodium dodecyl-sulfate polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis showing purified CFEM10 protein. B–D antimicrobial activity of purified CFEM10against B E. coli, C P. syringae pv. tomato DC3000, and D S. cerevisiae. Antimicrobial activity was determined by measuring the optical density of respective organisms after exposure to purified CFEM proteins with a final concentration of 8 µM in LB medium. LB medium mixed with elution buffer was used as a control treatment. * denotes statistically significant differences based on a t-test (p < 0.05). Error bars represent standard deviation based on eight biological replicates
figures.label: Fig. 3

figures.caption: Deletion of cfem10 affects C. rosea conidiation. Conidial production in the WT and Δcfem10 strains was determined at 10 dpi on PDA. Error bars represent standard deviation based on four biological replicates. Different letters indicate statistically significant differences (P ≤ 0.05) based on the Tukey-Kramer test
figures.label: Fig. 4
